models.collectorNote: 1969 Hemi cars sit at the classic peak; among modern cars, the 2023 'Last Call' Hellcats are the ones being put away. A clean 1968–70 440 car is the driver's buy.

generations.name: Charger R/T
generations.note: The Coke-bottle shape, the full-width grille, Bullitt's villain and the Dukes' hero. The 426 Hemi was the headline; the 440 Magnum was the street pick.

generations.name: Charger SRT Hellcat
generations.note: 707 hp in a family sedan rewrote the rules; the Redeye took it to 797. The Widebody of 2020 finally gave it the tyre the power always needed.

generations.name: Charger Daytona (electric)
generations.note: The eighth generation leads with the dual-motor Daytona (670 hp in Scat Pack form) and adds a twin-turbo 'Sixpack' six-cylinder. The market's verdict is still being written.

models.intro: From the 1968 car that defined the muscle silhouette, through two decades as a four-door sedan with Hellcat power, to the electric-and-six-cylinder Charger of 2024, the nameplate keeps reinventing the same idea.

models.collectorNote: Demons trade as collectibles already. The thinking buy is a manual Hellcat Widebody, the full experience at a third of Demon money.

generations.name: Challenger R/T
generations.note: One year of glory: 1970 offered everything from a slant six to the 426 Hemi, plus the T/A built for Trans-Am homologation. The 'Cuda's plusher twin.

generations.name: Challenger SRT Hellcat / Demon
generations.note: The Hellcat put 707 hp under $60k. The 2018 Demon, 840 hp, drag radials from the factory, banned by the NHRA for being too fast without a cage, and the 2023 Demon 170 closed the book.

models.intro: Late to the pony-car fight in 1970, gone by 1974, then reborn in 2008 as a full-size retro coupé that outlived its rivals, and ended with the 840 hp Demon and the 1,025 hp Demon 170.
models.name: Challenger

models.collectorNote: ACRs lead the market and Gen II GTS coupés are the rising value, the blue-and-white launch colours especially. All Vipers want a careful check for track and 'Viper tax' deferred maintenance.

generations.name: RT/10
generations.note: The Lamborghini-assisted alloy V10 made 400 hp and the car weighed 1,490 kg with plastic bodywork. Side curtains and a toupee roof; nothing about it was house-trained.

generations.name: Viper GTS / ACR
generations.note: The final car: 8.4 litres, 645 hp, and the ACR's aero package making a genuine tonne of downforce. ACRs took production-car records at 13 US tracks in one farewell tour.

models.intro: A V10, a tube frame, and no apology: no ABS, no traction control, no side windows on the first cars. Five generations of America's most honest sports car.
models.name: Viper

generations.name: Durango R/T / SRT Hellcat
generations.note: The third generation shares bones with the Grand Cherokee and kept the Hemi long after rivals downsized. SRT 392 and Hellcat trims are the enthusiast end; the platform soldiers on into the late 2020s.

models.intro: Three rows and a Hemi for most of its life. The SRT Hellcat version, 710 hp, briefly the most powerful production SUV in the world, turned the school run into a drag strip.
models.name: Durango
